title: Loved ones mourn man's death at London jail - the 22nd since 2009
article: A man who died after being found unresponsive in his cell at London's Elgin-Middlesex Detention Centre is being remembered as someone with a big personality and "good heart" who put his family first.
Neither London police nor Queen's Park officials have published the name of the inmate pronounced dead in hospital Friday, but friends and family have identified him as Bryan Michael Meyers.
Meyers liked to write songs and was a kind and caring guy who wore his heart on his sleeve, his sister said Sunday.

"His family meant a lot to him. Bryan could light up any room or place he walked into," Khala Kirsten-Anne Atkins wrote in a social-media message exchange with The Free Press. "Bryan was hilarious too. There was never a shortage of happiness when Bryan was around you."
Meyers had run-ins with the law over the years. Friend Steve Doyle said he was a quick-witted guy with many friends and an active social life.
"He always had an upbeat personality. He was always positive, no matter how negative the situation was," said Doyle, who was told of his friend's death by Meyers' girlfriend.

Meyers had been taken to hospital for pneumonia on Wednesday, Doyle said, and was sent back to the provincial jail on Exeter Road, where he was put in segregation instead of a general population range.
"Friday morning when they went to bring him his breakfast, they found him unresponsive," Doyle said.

London police and paramedics responded to the jail at about 7:30 a.m. Friday to reports of a man in medical distress. CPR was underway as paramedics raced to the scene, the initial emergency call said.

The man was rushed to hospital where he was later pronounced dead, police said. The department's major crime section is assisting the regional coroner's office with the investigation, London police said Friday. No further updates have been provided.
A spokesperson from the Ministry of the Solicitor General said Friday the man was found "unresponsive" in his cell and taken to hospital where he was pronounced dead.
Meyers is the 22nd Elgin-Middlesex Detention Centre inmate to die there since 2009, although none was reported in 2023.
Many of the inmate deaths over the years have been attributed to overdoses on drugs smuggled into the jail.

Coroner's inquests into previous deaths, which are mandatory in every inmate fatality at a provincial jail, have identified violence, understaffing, overcrowding, inadequate health care and inadequate supervision as significant issues at the jail.

In January 2023, following a review of the deaths in correctional custody between 2014 and 2021, a nine-person panel convened by Ontario's chief coroner released a report with recommendations on how to fix the province's "increasingly ineffective and unsafe" corrections system and prevent further deaths.
